column1: # One row per option: what the C sources cannot say. scripts/gen-options.sh reads this file and the sources; it fails when an option has no row. Defaults, ranges and contexts are read from the sources, never stored here.
# key: a setting (sift.name) or a reloption (kind(name)). applies: all, BM25, sift_col, sift_table (a list), or - for a deprecated alias that is not listed (the reason in buys).
# since: the release that added the option (3.3, 3.4); the last release of scripts/options-released.tsv has it by definition.
# group: settings of one family share a README row; a member takes every empty cell (buys, cost, class, why, evidence, pr, bench, advice) from the first row of the group.
# values: the grammar of a string option. minor: the column format minor the option writes (checked against SIFT_COL_FORMAT_MINOR). link: file#heading of docs/.
# The case of the option (rendered into docs/OPTIONS.md; scripts/gen-options.sh --missing lists what is not measured):
# class: default (on by default, or a knob whose default is the recommended value), opt-in, diagnostic, safety, deprecated.

# why: an opt-in only, the limit of the 3.3 rule for a default that it failed (gain: under 5% on a relevant class, growth: over 3% of the index, write: over 5% write cost) or result, hardware, memory, risk.
# gain, growth, write: the measurement with its conditions (rows, columns, version); `-` when the option has no such effect; empty when nobody measured it.
# pr: the pull requests that introduced or last changed the behaviour. bench: a case of bench/cases.tsv, or a file of docs/ (results/x.tsv, perf/x.md#heading), or `-`.
# advice: the line a user reads: when to set it, when to leave it, how to opt out.
